koynx.result: Three surfaces (mobile, web and admin) designed end to end on one design system. Every money-moving flow passed compliance review with zero redesign cycles, and new screens now start 70% done.
koynx.did: I led the design. I took Hillcross Pay through its rebrand to KOYNX, set up the design system, and designed the member app, the web app and the admin portal.
koynx.problem: South Africans save through banking apps, Esusu pots and stokvels kept in notebooks and on WhatsApp, and nothing shows them every rand in one place.

koynx-admin.result: One portal for every operations job: KYC in three tiers, risk ranked by severity, and role-based access, with every action logged by IP and timestamp.
koynx-admin.did: I designed the portal end to end on the KOYNX design system: sign-in, overview, users, savings, groups, transactions, KYC, support and risk, and sub-admins.
koynx-admin.problem: Staff had to verify members, watch every money flow and resolve risk without ever approving someone by accident.
koynx-admin.trade: Accept stays disabled until every KYC document is verified. Each review takes an extra step, but nobody gets approved by mistake.
koynx-admin.next: The portal launches with KOYNX in South Africa. Feedback from reviewers and risk staff goes back into the shared components.

hillcross.result: The intake year is now visible as soon as the page loads. Admissions entry points above the fold went from 2 to 4, and hero copy dropped from 63 words to 8.
hillcross.did: I redesigned the homepage hero: the intake announcement bar, an intake-led headline, two calls to action, real campus photography and a slider visitors can control.
hillcross.problem: The homepage welcomed visitors but never said that admissions were open, or for which year.
hillcross.trade: A slider lets the hero carry more than one story, but sliders can move content away from someone still reading. I added pause, a counter and controls, so the visitor stays in control.

hcstudent.result: One dashboard that always shows a student their next step, from Start Registration to their first module, with support on every view.
hcstudent.did: I redesigned the legacy student platform: the registration card and its three states, the e-portal assessment flow, and the components shared with the teacher and admin portals.
hcstudent.problem: New students saw every tool at once and didn't know what to do first.
hcstudent.trade: One primary action per state means fewer shortcuts on screen. In return, a new student never has to guess what comes next.

hcteacher.result: Signing in now answers three questions on one screen: how the class is doing, what needs grading and what has changed.
hcteacher.did: I redesigned the legacy teacher portal: the overview, the engagement panel, the grading queue, lesson completion rows and empty states.
hcteacher.problem: The old portal stored records but gave lecturers no sense of what mattered today.
hcteacher.trade: Showing zeros and empty states instead of hiding cards makes a new account look sparse. In return the layout never changes, so a teacher learns it once.

hcportal.result: 13 student flows designed end to end, from first application to exam day, on one design system that the lecturer and admin portals will share.
hcportal.did: I designed the student portal and the system behind all three portals: applications with a live APS score and ID checks, an adaptive dashboard, AI study planning, proctored exams and finance.
hcportal.problem: Students needed one place to apply, register, study and pay, instead of paperwork and queues.
hcportal.trade: AI Assist suggests a task order instead of setting the plan for the student. It's less automatic, but the student stays in charge of their day.

wemove.result: A seven-step onboarding that ends in the first reward, and a collectible mint system that testers said gave them a reason not to skip a day.
wemove.did: As UI/UX designer, I designed onboarding, home and profile, workouts, Quick Burst and rewards, plus the visual language and style guide.
wemove.problem: People needed a reason to come back tomorrow, not just a log of what they did today.
wemove.trade: Giving a mint before the first workout spends a reward early. It also teaches the reward system on day one, which mattered more.

lucenture.result: A live four-page site with a booking flow, where Book a call is always within reach and every service says who it's for.
lucenture.did: I designed the brand and wordmark, the visual language and the website: home, services, case studies, about, booking and contact.
lucenture.problem: Small business owners couldn't tell which consulting service fit them without calling first.
lucenture.trade: Dark team photography in the hero sets a premium tone but competes with the text. I darkened the photos so the message leads.

heatbud.result: Live and installable: feels-like temperature, a seven-day heat forecast, a personal water plan and three ways to be reminded.
heatbud.did: I designed, built and shipped it myself, from the research and UI to the PWA, push alerts and deployment.
heatbud.problem: Weather apps show a number, not what it means for your day: when to go out and how much to drink.

blissbill.result: Seven flows designed end to end in light and dark mode, from sign-up and identity checks to bill payments and a virtual card.
blissbill.did: I took the flat first concept and redesigned it: home, sign-up, NIN, BVN and selfie checks, bill flows, the virtual card, and a full dark mode built on the same tokens.
blissbill.problem: Paying small, frequent bills meant juggling apps, USSD codes and agents.
blissbill.trade: A full dark mode doubled the states to design and maintain. Most sessions happen at night, so it was in scope from day one.

laundromate.result: A complete booking app with 8 flows. Prices show in local currency before sign-up, and the receipt matches the review screen line for line.
laundromate.did: I designed the app end to end: onboarding, location-based prices, services that stack in one order, scheduled pickup and delivery, checkout and receipt.
laundromate.problem: Laundry services hide prices until you call, and pickup times are hard to pin down.
laundromate.trade: Showing prices before an account means some visitors leave without signing up. Testers said it was the reason they stayed.
